diagnosis.root_cause: The customer's ONU is definitely offline and deregistered (online: 0, MPCP DEREG), with the outage beginning around 16:09. The available history shows stable optical levels and bias current before the ONU stopped reporting, so there is no evidence of fibre or laser degradation.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds but reports online: 0, auth_flag Una uth, and MPCP DEREG; this is a definite offline ONU result, not a monitoring timeout.
The target ONU is the only offline ONU among the sampled EPON0/4 peers; the other six peers are online with normal RX power and TX power.
The OLT responds to both ping and SNMP, and its CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are healthy, ruling out an OLT failure.
Surviving customers on the same PON port rule out a whole-port failure and, with only one definite negative, rule out a splitter failure.

Historical RX power remained in the normal band around -21 to -22 dBm, TX power stayed near the healthy 2.3 dBm mean, distance remained constant at 133, and TX bias stayed healthy and flat; fibre degradation, laser degradation, and distance change are unsupported.

The RADIUS record is present and CRM-consistent, the expected customer VLAN 1094 is present, and the router heartbeat is healthy, so authentication, provisioning, VLAN, router, and upstream infrastructure are not the cause.
The OLT health result claiming all seven PONs failed contradicts the live per-ONU results and healthy OLT access; it is a false critical monitoring condition and should be corrected separately.

remediation.action: Dispatch or contact the customer to verify ONU power and cabling, reboot the ONU, and inspect the customer drop/fibre and ONU hardware. Replace or re-register the ONU if it does not return online. After recovery, verify normal RX/TX readings and traffic. Separately correct the OLT health check, which is falsely marking all PONs failed despite successful OLT access and mostly online ONUs.

ground_truth.root_cause: This customer's ONU has genuinely deregistered, with a clean signal history up to the cut-off. The OLT's concurrent critical health alarm is a separate false positive: the live probe answers normally for every other ONU on the port, so the health check result does not reflect the device state.
expected_reasoning: The customer's ONU returns responds true with online 0, a definite offline answer
Signal history was flat and healthy until the cut-off four hours ago, so power loss or ONU failure is indicated
The OLT health record separately reports critical with all PONs failed
However the live probe answers normally for every other ONU on EPON0/4, returning real RX and TX values
OLT ping and SNMP both succeed, uptime is 44 days, and CPU, memory and temperature are at baseline
If the OLT or its PON ports had genuinely failed, no ONU would be responding and many more customers would be offline
CRM shows the OLT's offline count consistent with the normal background rate, not a mass outage
The health alarm is therefore a false critical and must not be conflated with this customer's real fault
Two findings coexist: one genuine single-customer outage and one monitoring defect

expected_escalation.review_reason: A concurrent false critical health alarm on this OLT should be raised separately with monitoring

distractors: The critical OLT alarm invites attributing the customer outage to an OLT failure
Dismissing the alarm too readily risks also dismissing the genuine customer fault
Only one customer is affected despite an alarm claiming the whole OLT
